AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is a compost heap turned with a fork? (1 mark)
   A. To remove all the water
   B. To let in air and mix the materials
   C. To add plastic
   D. To make it smaller

2. Which of these helps to prevent soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   B. Leaving the ground bare
   C. Burning the soil
   D. Digging up all the plants

3. Which of these crops can be watered with drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Only trees in forests
   B. Nothing at all
   C. Only crops under water
   D. Tomatoes in rows

4. Where is the neck of the bottle placed in a bottle drip system? (1 mark)
   A. On the leaves
   B. High in a tree
   C. In the bucket
   D. In the soil beside the plant

5. Why should the end of the drip pipe be closed? (1 mark)
   A. So water does not run out of the end
   B. So rainwater cannot enter
   C. So the pipe looks nice
   D. So the plants do not drink

6. Why does a lid on a pot save fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It stops the food from cooking
   B. It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   C. It cools the food
   D. It makes the pot lighter

7. What should you do after the water starts to boil? (1 mark)
   A. Turn the flame down or move wood back
   B. Add paraffin
   C. Open the pot and blow on it
   D. Add more wood

8. What should the scarecrow pole be like? (1 mark)
   A. Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   B. Loose so it can fall over
   C. Very short
   D. Made of glass

9. Which tool gives gentle watering of a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. Cup thrown from far
   B. Bucket poured fast
   C. Hose without a nozzle
   D. Watering can with a fine rose

10. Why do we mix tiny seeds with dry sand? (1 mark)
   A. To kill germs
   B. To make them wet
   C. To spread them thinly and evenly
   D. To make them heavy

11. Why do crowded seedlings grow badly? (1 mark)
   A. They like company
   B. They compete for water, light and food
   C. They have no roots
   D. They get too much space

12. How far should mulch be from the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Not needed
   B. A small gap away
   C. Piled tightly against it
   D. Ten metres

13. Which of these fruits does best in cool highland areas? (1 mark)
   A. Cashew nut
   B. Mango
   C. Tree tomato
   D. Coconut

14. Which practice keeps children safe when harvesting fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Push each other
   B. Pull the branch down hard
   C. Use a picking pole and take turns
   D. Climb all trees

15. What is a grafted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A dead plant
   B. A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   C. A seed in a bag
   D. A plant grown in water

16. Which of these is a climbing fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Guava
   B. Orange
   C. Mango
   D. Grapes

17. How does manure from animals help crops? (1 mark)
   A. It supplies plant food to the soil
   B. It gives shade
   C. It scares birds
   D. It makes crops small

18. What does variety mean in eating? (1 mark)
   A. Eating slowly
   B. Eating a lot
   C. Eating many different kinds of food
   D. Eating one food only

19. Which of these is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali
   B. Sukuma wiki
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Sugar

20. Which of these meals is balanced? (1 mark)
   A. Chips only
   B. Tea and bread only
   C. Soda and sweets
   D. Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki

21. What do body-building foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Only give heat
   B. Only quench thirst
   C. Help the body to grow and repair
   D. Make food taste sweet

22. Which of these foods needs a long time of boiling before it is soft enough to eat? (1 mark)
   A. Tomato
   B. Cucumber
   C. Dry beans
   D. Ripe banana

23. Which kitchen item helps to turn food in a pan? (1 mark)
   A. A spatula
   B. A sieve
   C. A bucket
   D. A ladle only

24. What should you do if oil in a pan catches fire? (1 mark)
   A. Carry the pan outside quickly
   B. An adult covers the pan with a lid and turns off the heat
   C. Blow on it
   D. Pour water on it

25. What should be placed under a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A bed
   B. A basin or a soak pit
   C. A plant only
   D. A radio

26. How can you make drinking water safe? (1 mark)
   A. Boil it and let it cool covered
   B. Leave it in the sun uncovered
   C. Stir it with a stick
   D. Add soil

27. Which PPE is worn on the feet at school and in the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Canvas shoes
   B. Gloves
   C. Overall
   D. Dust mask

28. Why should chemicals not be used to clean PPE unless an adult directs you? (1 mark)
   A. They are too cheap
   B. They can harm the skin and the material
   C. They make it too clean
   D. They cool the PPE

29. Why should rubber boots not be dried in very strong heat? (1 mark)
   A. They become cleaner
   B. The rubber can crack
   C. They get heavier
   D. They grow

30. Which is a type of tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Cross stitch
   B. Even tacking
   C. Satin stitch
   D. Chain stitch

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Plan a class display of cleaned PPE. Say what you would show and what information cards you would write. (5 marks)

32. Why should a thread colour different from the cloth be used? (2 marks)

33. Explain four ways in which wild animals help people or the environment. (4 marks)

34. Design a hygiene log for one week. List five practices to record and explain how you will use it. (5 marks)

35. Why is tacking better than pins alone? (2 marks)

36. Explain how stagnant water around the home can lead to disease and how to prevent it. (4 marks)

37. Give three uses of sheep. (3 marks)

38. Name three improvised cleaning tools and what each is made from. (3 marks)

39. Give three reasons why a clean home is important. (3 marks)

40. State the functions of roots, leaves and flowers in a fruit tree. (3 marks)

41. Explain how PPE should be stored and why. (4 marks)

42. Describe how to boil potatoes. (4 marks)

43. List four safety rules when cooking. (4 marks)

44. Explain what is meant by a balanced meal. (2 marks)

45. Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — To let in air and mix the materials
   Mixing brings outer material to the middle so all rots evenly.

2. A — Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   Covering keeps rain from washing soil away.

3. D — Tomatoes in rows
   Drip systems suit row crops such as tomatoes and kale.

4. D — In the soil beside the plant
   The bottle is buried neck down near the plant.

5. A — So water does not run out of the end
   An open end would waste water.

6. B — It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   Less heat escapes so less fuel is used.

7. A — Turn the flame down or move wood back
   A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

8. A — Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   A loose pole falls in the wind.

9. D — Watering can with a fine rose
   Fine spray does not wash seeds away.

10. C — To spread them thinly and evenly
   Sand helps prevent clumps of seeds.

11. B — They compete for water, light and food
   Too many plants in a small space fight for resources.

12. B — A small gap away
   Mulch touching the stem can cause rot.

13. C — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato grows well in cooler highlands, while coconut, cashew and mango like warm places.

14. C — Use a picking pole and take turns
   Use safe methods.

15. B — A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   Grafted trees give good quality fruit sooner.

16. D — Grapes
   Grapes grow on vines.

17. A — It supplies plant food to the soil
   Manure enriches the soil.

18. C — Eating many different kinds of food
   Variety means different foods.

19. B — Sukuma wiki
   Vegetables give vitamins and minerals.

20. D — Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki
   It includes all three groups.

21. C — Help the body to grow and repair
   They are rich in protein.

22. C — Dry beans
   Dry beans are hard and need long cooking.

23. A — A spatula
   A spatula lifts and turns food.

24. B — An adult covers the pan with a lid and turns off the heat
   Water makes an oil fire worse.

25. B — A basin or a soak pit
   To catch the dirty water.

26. A — Boil it and let it cool covered
   Boiling kills germs.

27. A — Canvas shoes
   Canvas shoes protect feet.

28. B — They can harm the skin and the material
   Chemicals can be dangerous.

29. B — The rubber can crack
   Heat damages rubber.

30. B — Even tacking
   Even tacking is taught in Grade 4.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Display gloves, gumboots, mask, headgear, overall, canvas shoes; cards say what each protects and how to clean it; safe storage; explain to visitors.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for items, 2 marks for cards, 1 mark for explaining.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: The stitches are easy to see and to remove.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Birds eat insects; bees pollinate; animals spread seeds; wildlife brings tourists and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Practices: washed hands before meals, brushed teeth twice, bathed, clean clothes, drank safe water. Tick each day, count ticks at the end, and improve the practice with fewest ticks.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for practices and table, 2 marks for use.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Pins can slip or prick, tacking holds cloth firmly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mosquitoes breed in it and spread malaria. Empty tins and tyres, fill puddles, and drain water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for breeding, 1 mark for disease, 2 marks for prevention.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mutton, wool (some breeds), skins, manure, income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Duster from old cloth; mop from strips of cloth on a stick; dustpan from a cut jerrican.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each tool with material.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: It prevents diseases, keeps food safe, prevents accidents and looks pleasant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the tree and take in water; leaves make food using sunlight; flowers form fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean and dry, in a cupboard, rack or clean box, so it does not grow mould or spread germs, and labelled so it is used by the owner.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for storing, 2 marks for reasons.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash, peel and cut into equal pieces; put in a pot with water and salt; cover and boil for about 15 to 20 minutes until soft; drain the water carefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A meal that has foods from all the main food groups in the right amounts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for foods from all groups, 1 mark for right amounts.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.
